# Maintainer review

Before merging each PR, inspect its final diff and tested commit, including changes by maintainers. Verify the submitting GitHub account matches the folder and each credited profile belongs to the named contributor. Review every specific byline in the workflow and generated README against the actual work; include coauthors where applicable, and confirm that each person agrees to public attribution. Review idea-only or collaborator credit for opt-in with the person concerned. Do not invent names, work or adoption. A correction needs review with affected contributors. Keep the credit record and its readable description when an entry is renamed or retired, as described in CONTRIBUTING.md. Verify the generated README links and run the offline checks.

Review provenance separately for original prose, examples and third-party components, including licenses and required attribution. Check employer authority, material AI-assisted provenance, private or client data, marks and any implication of endorsement. A public issue or discussion does not authorize republication. If evidence is missing or a privacy concern arises, stop the affected merge and refer it to the repository owner without posting sensitive material publicly. Arrange a private exchange for rights evidence. Security vulnerability reports belong in the repository’s Security tab.

Before merging, link the [certification](../CONTRIBUTOR-CERTIFICATION.md) at the governing base commit and record the final reviewed PR head. For the policy transition itself, the current base terms remain in force.

1. Verify that the submitter personally affirmed the certification for their own work or has authority to act for the identified rights holder. Review the PR description and its edit history. A valid first line, original account or latest editor cannot establish who made a particular edit, authority or intent. When unclear, ask the submitter for a fresh, explicit confirmation in a comment from their own account. Never confirm on another person's behalf.
2. Check sources, licenses, AI-assisted provenance and required credits. For each additional rights holder whose permission is needed, verify their own confirmation and scope, or verify the representative's authority. Check newly credited coauthors' comment links, account names, description of work and consent to credit. Verify private evidence privately. Record the public verification outcome without disclosing sensitive details.
3. Recheck the final diff and rights holders after changes. Obtain fresh confirmation if rights, authorship or certification terms change. If authorization is uncertain, hold the PR.

The required **Contributor agreement** status keeps its historical name for branch protection. Its trusted-base checker reads the current PR on GitHub and requires the v1 checkbox on the first line, the expected human account and head, and a compatible latest-editor record. It does not authenticate a signature or establish consent, authorship, coauthor permission or third-party rights. Prefer comments when suggesting description edits. If a different account edits the description, ask the submitter to personally review it, then clear and recheck the box if accurate. An edit to the PR description or a pushed commit refreshes the check. New commits can leave an existing checkbox checked, so inspect the final diff, including commits made by other accounts. If the API fails, the check fails closed.

Preserve original Git commit authors when merging. Use appropriately consented `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailers for genuine coauthors, with an email each person agrees to publish, such as their GitHub-provided no-reply address. Never disclose a private email to create attribution. GitHub may recognize contributors when the associated commit email is linked to their account; its contributor graph and recognition are not guaranteed. Check the merge method and resulting history. For squash or rebase, link the final reviewed PR commit to the resulting default-branch commit and verify that the accepted content and intended authors survived. Do not replace specific repository bylines with a contributor graph.

The CI scope and agreement checks are read-only signals, not substitutes for this review. Protect the base workflow, trusted scripts, CODEOWNERS and policy with required owner review and required checks in repository settings. Require branches to be up to date before merging so the generated credits include intervening merges, then rerun the checks. Confirm these protections work for fork PRs. The pull request event reads the proposed workflow definition. A passing check name is insufficient if the PR changes that definition. Inspect all workflow, ownership and trusted-script diffs against the base before approving a workflow run or merge. Outside submissions that touch them must be rejected, even if GitHub shows a green check. Never execute contributor-proposed scripts with privileged credentials, and do not add token writes.
